taxonomyNote: NatureServe notes some authors consider it conspecific with O. leucogaster.
fieldMarks: Large, long-tailed, small-headed; 50-66 cm, 680 g-1.1 kg
Dull olive brown, greyer head, buff belly; may show red on the throat
Wide black tail feathers with white tips; sexes similar
behavior: Loud, raucous 'cha-cha-lac', often in chorus at dawn and dusk; male's voice lower than female's
Forages on the ground or in shrubs and trees, climbing about in thin branches
Mostly vegetarian: berries (coyotillo, pigeonberry, hackberry), seeds, leaves, buds, flowers; a few insects and snails
Nest is a stick platform 4-15 ft up in dense cover
habitat: Subtropical woods, river groves and dense brush, usually near water in south Texas; native ebony, hackberry, huisache and mesquite woodland and overgrown orchard edges.
range: Extreme southern Texas (Rio Grande Valley) south through Mexico and Central America; NatureServe also records it in Georgia.
